newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Profitability of Israeli industrial firms falls.
newsitem.headline: Profitability of Israeli industrial firms falls.

text.p: Publicly traded Israeli industrial companies saw operating profitability fall sharply in the first nine months of 1996, the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) said on Wednesday.

The survey of 189 TASE-listed companies found that operating profit as a percent of equity fell to 14.6 percent in January-September, compared with 19.1 percent in the year earlier period and 16.4 percent for all of 1995.
As a percentage of revenues, operating profits fell to 6.9 percent from 8.4 percent a year earlier.
The TASE noted that in past years the fourth quarter tended to show lower profitability than the first nine months so that full-year 1996 profitability would likely to show a further deterioration.

The only companies to run against the trend were those that adjust their financial reports to the dollar. Among those 31 companies, the TASE found that operating profit as a percentage of equity rose to 18.1 percent in the nine months, compared with 16.9 percent a year earlier and 15.6 percent for full-year 1995.
The dollar-linked companies are export-oriented and many of them are high technology companies.
